A.name: AREEYA PROPERTY PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
A.thesis: Distressed property developer in deepening losses (FY25 net loss THB 1,248.9mn vs THB 426.4mn FY24) with multiple loan/debenture defaults and equity nearly wiped — solvency, not earnings, is the issue.
A.summary: Areeya Property is in financial distress. FY2025 revenue collapsed 49% YoY to THB 712.8mn and net loss widened to THB 1,248.9mn (FY24: -426.4mn), driving D/E to 10.6x and equity down to THB 1,215.7mn. Q1-2026 deteriorated further: revenue THB 132.9mn, net loss THB 290.5mn, equity THB 921.9mn, D/E 14.3x and quick ratio 0.02 — effectively no liquidity. FS notes confirm defaults on interest to individuals/companies (THB 43mn + 8mn) and on debentures (THB 35mn post period-end), triggering creditors' acceleration rights; the company is renegotiating extensions with 3 banks and relies on a THB 255mn director loan (due-at-call, with a non-recall confirmation). The 9 Jun 2026 asset-disposal memorandum and repeated AGM cancellations suggest active restructuring/asset sales to survive. Stock at 52-week low, -40% YTD. This is a turnaround/survival situation requiring close covenant and going-concern monitoring.
A.business: Property developer offering single-detached houses, townhouses and condominiums (sells land and/or built houses), plus the Pickadaily Bangkok community mall. Sector PROP; market cap THB 2.84bn.

A5.name: ASSET FIVE GROUP PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
A5.thesis: Property holding company whose earnings have sharply de-rated — FY25 net profit fell 77% to THB 102.9mn and Q1-2026 swung to a THB 11.9mn loss — leaving the stock expensive (PE 35x) on a shrinking base.
A5.summary: Asset Five Group is a real-estate holding company whose performance has deteriorated materially. FY2025 revenue fell 27% YoY to THB 1,317.0mn and net profit dropped 77% to THB 102.9mn (FY24: 453.3mn), with NPM compressing to 7.8% from 25.0% and gross margin to 31.0% from 43.1%. The MD&A attributes the decline to lower real estate sales (-26.2%), a 64.8% fall in operating profit, and the disappearance of joint-venture profit contribution (FY24 included a THB 73.5mn JV impairment, now nil). Q1-2026 turned to a net loss of THB 11.9mn on THB 216.2mn revenue with negative EBITDA, though operating cash flow stayed positive (THB 31.6mn) and investing inflows were strong (THB 199.6mn). The balance sheet remains sound (D/E 1.18x, current ratio 4.1x, equity THB 1,670.8mn). Valuation looks stretched at PE 35.3x given the earnings decline; tone is Watch on the >10% profit fall and Q1 loss.
A5.business: Holding company investing in real estate and related businesses (subsidiaries, JVs, associates). Sector PROP; market cap THB 2.20bn; pays a dividend (FY25 DY ~5.4%, current 2.75%).

AAI.name: Asian Alliance International Public Company Limited
AAI.thesis: Thai pet-food OEM with strong demand volume but FX-driven margin collapse and three HIGH-flag RPT/concentration items in the 2026Q1 digest that must clear before escalation.
AAI.summary: AAI posted Q1/2026 revenue of THB 1,604mn (sales THB 1,558mn, -17.1% YoY) with net profit THB 137.5mn (-46.9% YoY but +25.3% QoQ). GP margin compressed to 11.2% from 18.5% a year earlier, driven by USD weakness against THB (~80% of revenue is USD) and lower fixed-cost absorption as US/Canada customers cut orders ahead of tariffs (US/Canada share fell from ~57% to ~47%). FY2025 already showed the structural strain: GPM dropped 20.4%->15.1% and net profit fell 26.2% to THB 740.7mn, with FY2026 GPM guidance set at only 13-16%. The most material flags sit in the 2026Q1 filing digest: three HIGH items — related-party raw-material purchases up 3.5x YoY with no named counterparty, short-term loans to parent ASIAN with THB 932.8mn single-quarter gross flow needing a Size Test, and two undisclosed US/Canada customers at 44.2% of revenue. Balance sheet remains conservative (D/E 0.18x, current ratio 6.0x), DY ~9.6%.
AAI.business: OEM manufacturer and distributor of wet pet food (~88% of revenue), shelf-stable human/tuna food, and tuna by-products. Exports-led; key markets US/Canada (~47-57%), Europe ~22%, Middle East. ~70% owned by Asian Sea Corporation (ASIAN). New Building 3 lifts wet pet food capacity to 64,000 tonnes by 2026.

AIMCG.name: AIM COMMERCIAL GROWTH FREEHOLD AND LEASEHOLD REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST
AIMCG.thesis: Small mixed-use/office REIT in turnaround after resolving the D-Land default, but with suspended/capital-reduction distributions, falling revenue and a deep discount to NAV (PBV 0.17) — recovery hinges on execution and the Rama II catalyst.
AIMCG.summary: AIMCG is a small Bangkok mixed-use/office REIT (UD Town, 72 Courtyard now 'ROW 55', Porto Chino, Noble Solo) trading at a steep discount (PBV 0.17, price THB 1.36, -22.7% YTD). FY2025 total revenue fell to THB 265.4mn (from 315.9mn FY24) and net investment income declined ~16% YoY to ~THB 68mn, driven by expiry of revenue-undertaking on UD Town/Porto Chino, rental-rate cuts and tenant exits. The major positive is resolution of the D-Land asset-manager default: the D-Land receivable was written down from THB 129mn to 0 and Thonglor Management (TLM) took over. However, the REIT booked a THB 48.5mn ECL provision in Q2-2025 and deferred Q3/Q4 2025 distributions to preserve liquidity for renovation capex; recent disclosures (11 Jun 2026 capital reduction; 11 May distribution-as-capital-reduction) confirm distributions are now structured as capital returns. Q1-2026 revenue THB 65.3mn. Yield (~3.7%) trails industrial-REIT peers. Watch given HIGH-severity capital-reduction events, suspended distributions and ongoing execution risk.
AIMCG.business: REIT holding leasehold/sublease rights in UD Town, 72 Courtyard (renamed ROW 55) and Porto Chino, plus commercial condo ownership in Noble Solo. Mixed-use/commercial and office space; leasehold ~27.2 years remaining. Manager: AIM Real Estate Management. Sector PF&REIT; market cap THB 392mn.

AKS.name: AKS CORPORATION PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
AKS.thesis: Effectively a delisting-watch situation: negative equity (THB -207.3mn), penny-stock price (THB 0.02), suspended (SP) for failing to file Q1-2026 financials, with cancelled AGM and suspended dividend — distress, not investability.
AKS.summary: AKS Corporation is in severe distress and trading is impaired. The most recent full-period figures (FY2025, 12-month) show revenue THB 209.9mn, a net loss of THB 315.1mn, negative EBITDA of THB 248.7mn and, critically, negative shareholders' equity of THB -207.3mn against total liabilities of THB 4,412.6mn — i.e., the company is balance-sheet insolvent. ROE -242%, gross margin -168% and current ratio 0.27 confirm an unviable cost structure and no liquidity. The shares (THB 0.02) carry an SP suspension sign posted 18 May 2026 for failure to submit financial statements for the period ending 31 March 2026, plus a CF sign and cash-balance trading restriction. The Board has suspended dividends and cancelled the 2026 AGM, and there have been repeated director resignations/appointments. With market cap, PE, PBV and the latest financials all null in the context, this is a survival/possible-delisting case rather than a coverage candidate; primary filings are not yet available because the company has not filed.

ALLY.name: ALLY FREEHOLD AND LEASEHOLD REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST
ALLY.thesis: Stable, well-occupied retail (community-mall) REIT with >90% occupancy and conservative gearing (0.27), trading at a deep discount to NAV (PBV 0.47) with a high ~9-12% yield; two new assets in Q1-2026 should lift the revenue base.
ALLY.summary: ALLY is a retail REIT holding 15 community-mall assets (The Crystal chain and Sammakorn Place malls) across Bangkok and vicinity. It is operationally stable: occupancy has held above 90% for ~10 years including through COVID, gearing is a conservative ~0.27x, and FY2025 revenue was THB 1,597.0mn (broadly flat vs THB 1,616.8mn FY24). Q1-2026 revenue was THB 382.6mn; total assets THB 13,660.3mn, total liabilities THB 4,908.3mn. The REIT trades at a steep discount to book (PBV 0.47) with an attractive distribution yield (current ~9.4%, FY25 ~12.0%) and declared a Q1/2026 DPU of THB 0.1110/unit. Two new assets — The Crystal Ekamai-Ramindra and Crystal Design Center — were added in Q1-2026, expected to step up the revenue base and support DPU. Key risks are e-commerce pressure on tenants, lease-renewal exposure in 2026-2028, and a slight QoQ core revenue softening (-2.8%). P&L, equity and cash-flow detail are not in the context (REIT P&L line items null), so the tone is Neutral pending verification.

Sector PF&REIT (Retail REIT); market cap THB 4.13bn.

AMATAR.name: AMATA SUMMIT GROWTH FREEHOLD AND LEASEHOLD REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST
AMATAR.thesis: Stable industrial-factory REIT with flat-but-resilient rental income and improving net investment income (+9.8% YoY in Q1-2026 from cost declines), offering an ~8.3% yield at a discount to NAV (PBV 0.70).
AMATAR.summary: AMATAR is an industrial REIT holding freehold and leasehold rights to 88 factory buildings in Amata City Chonburi and Amata City Rayong industrial estates. Operations are stable: Q1-2026 rental income was THB 103,368 thousand (essentially flat, -0.7% YoY), reflecting stable occupancy, while net investment income (increase in net assets from operations) rose 9.8% YoY to THB 80,325 thousand. The improvement was cost-driven — REIT manager fees fell 58.9% YoY (THB 10,393k to 4,275k) and finance costs fell 32.2% (THB 8,014k to 5,433k) in line with lower THOR market rates — cutting total expenses ~25.9%. The balance sheet is steady (Q1-2026 total assets THB 4,706.4mn, total liabilities THB 1,024.1mn). The REIT yields ~8.3% (FY25 ~8.6%), trades at PBV 0.70 and is +7.4% YTD at THB 7.25. FY2025 revenue THB 418.4mn slightly exceeded FY24 (THB 407.8mn). With no HIGH flags and improving distributable income, the tone is Positive, with loan covenants (IBD/Total Assets, IBD/EBITDA) the main item to verify.
AMATAR.business: Industrial REIT investing in freehold and leasehold rights of 88 factory-building units in Amata City Chonburi and Amata City Rayong Industrial Estates. Manager-driven ready-built-factory leasing model. Sector PF&REIT (Industrial REIT); market cap THB 2.59bn.

AMATAV.thesis: AMATA's Vietnam IE holding company swung to a small Q1/2026 net loss as land sales collapsed 99%; the FY2025 turnaround margin was one-time-driven, and a HIGH revenue/loss flag plus missing NOTES extract warrant caution.
AMATAV.summary: AMATAV reported Q1/2026 revenue of THB 707.9mn (-17.9% YoY) and swung to a net loss of THB -2.8mn (vs +THB 5.2mn prior year, -153% YoY), with GP margin down to 8.1% and NPM -0.2%. The driver: land sales fell ~99% QoQ to just THB 1mn; utility revenue rose ~80% in VND but the weak dong cut THB-translated utility revenue ~3%. The 2026Q1 digest carries a HIGH flag on the revenue decline and loss swing, plus MED flags on US Section 301 tariff/forced-labour investigation risk and Vietnam inflation at 4.65% (3-year high). FY2025 looked strong on paper — net profit +398% to THB 459.8-531mn and group GPM up to 29.3% from 14.4% — but the digest flags the real-estate margin surge to 66.69% as one-time (THB 215mn ACHL cost rebasing, non-recurring) and notes THB 6.3bn prepaid land-use rights pending title transfer. Lumpy land sales (24.3ha vs 75.0ha) drive the volatility. Management guides Q2/Q3 recovery on 30+ha contracted plus 40ha LOI; FY2026 land-sale target 550 rai. Trades at PE 4.69x, PBV 0.40x.
AMATAV.business: Holding company (subsidiary of AMATA) developing industrial estates in Vietnam via AMATA City Bien Hoa, Long Thanh (ACLT) and Ha Long (ACHL). Revenue ~64% utility services, ~36% real-estate land sales. Long Thanh Airport Phase 1 is a key ACLT catalyst; QTIP (associate) contributes share-of-profit.

AP.summary: AP (Thailand) is a leading property developer, self-styled low-rise presales market leader. It is fundamentally sound but in a softening cycle. FY2025 net profit fell ~14% YoY to THB 4,316.7mn (FY24: 5,020.1mn) on roughly flat revenue (THB 37,625.9mn), with gross margin slipping to 31.9% (FY24 34.3%) amid heavy price promotions and construction-cost inflation. Q1-2026 was solid: net profit THB 903.5mn on revenue THB 9,590.2mn (+24% YoY IFRS / +11% management basis incl. 100% JV), six projects sold out (THB 6,175mn), and a visible condo backlog of THB 21,150mn from five FY26-transfer projects. Balance sheet is healthy (net D/E ~0.64x cited; reported D/E 0.87x, current ratio 4.4x, ROE ~9.5%) and the stock is cheap (PE ~5x, PBV 0.47, DY ~7.4%). The key flagged risk is a HIGH item: THB 2,000mn of debentures (AP267B+A) maturing July 2026 requiring confirmed refinancing, plus JV-related-party-transaction governance. GPM compression (~160-240bps) and a Krungsri FY26 profit downgrade temper the outlook. Tone Neutral.

APCS.summary: APCS is deeply impaired. FY2025 net loss attributable to the parent reached THB 498.3mn, up ~781% from THB 56.6mn, cutting equity 29.4% to THB 1,221.5mn. The 2025FY digest carries three HIGH flags: the loss magnitude; an auditor Emphasis of Matter on THB 192mn impairment of Bitcoin-mining assets (carrying value down to just THB 31mn); and the EPC segment's second straight year of operating loss (THB 203.7mn vs THB 185.6mn). Q1/2026 remained loss-making — revenue THB 148.6mn, EBITDA THB -54.5mn, net loss THB -86.3mn (EPS -0.13), GPM -7.3%, with negative ROE (-37.8%). Three business lines (EPC, raw-water/utilities, Bitcoin mining) all deteriorated, hit by the April 2024 Bitcoin halving, weak raw-water demand, and global headwinds. Recent disclosures show bondholders' meetings for APCS246A/APCS24NA being postponed, raising refinancing concern. KAM on percentage-of-completion construction revenue adds estimation risk. PBV 0.85x, no PE (loss-making), no dividend.

APURE.name: AGRIPURE HOLDINGS PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
APURE.thesis: FY25 swung to a THB 232.7mn net loss (NPM -11.7%) on a 9.1% sales decline, and an ongoing ECL provisioning review keeps risk elevated despite a Q1/26 return to small profit.
APURE.summary: AgriPure Holdings is a Thai agro-products holding company (canned sweet corn, fresh produce, commercial seed). FY2025 was a sharp reversal: sales fell 9.1% to THB 1,952.4mn, EBITDA turned negative (THB -140.0mn vs +421.3mn), and the group posted a net loss of THB 232.7mn (EPS -0.24) against a THB 278.3mn profit in 2024 — pre-tax profit swung -196.5% YoY. Gross margin compressed from 26.6% to 19.8%. Q1/2026 shows a tentative recovery: revenue THB 470.2mn, net profit THB 11.9mn (NPM 2.7%), with operating cash flow of THB 55.1mn. The balance sheet remains conservative (D/E 0.19x, current ratio 2.9x, equity THB 2,163mn). However, a 12-June-2026 disclosure on expected-credit-loss (ECL) provisioning progress for Q1/2026 signals unresolved receivables/credit risk. Trading at 0.89x PBV with no current P/E (trailing loss). Stance is Watch pending confirmation that the Q1 turnaround is durable.
APURE.business: Holding company operating through Thai subsidiaries in manufacturing and distribution of agro products — canned sweet corn, fresh vegetables and fruit, and commercial seed. Sector: FOOD. RM: Pim.

ASIAN.name: ASIAN SEA CORPORATION PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
ASIAN.thesis: Diversified Thai food group with a fortress balance sheet but FX-driven margin compression; Q1/2026 net profit fell 38.2% YoY on a sharp GP-margin drop, and FY2025 dividends-plus-capex outran operating cash flow.
ASIAN.summary: ASIAN posted Q1/2026 revenue of THB 2,489.9mn (sales THB 2,408.3mn, -10.5% YoY, -18.2% QoQ) and net profit THB 125.5mn (-38.2% YoY). GP margin fell sharply to 10.7% from 15.9%, on a product-mix shift to lower-margin items and higher raw-material/energy costs in pet food and frozen seafood. FY2025 showed the same structural strain: revenue flat at THB 10,948mn but GPM down to 13.8% from 17.6% (-3.8pp) and net profit -19.6% to THB 681.8mn, as a strong baht capped export pricing. The FY2025 digest carries MED flags: cash fell 82% to THB 153mn after THB 1,103mn dividends + THB 584mn capex exceeded THB 1,050mn operating cash flow; and THB 183mn of trade receivables aged 12 months concentrated 93% in one subsidiary (ECL allowance THB 129mn). Pet food remains the growth engine (volume +16.1% FY2025). Balance sheet is very strong (D/E 0.15x, current ratio 5.3x). Management guides FY2026 group revenue +10.8% to THB 11,927mn and GPM 13-15%, with a challenging +47% aqua-feed target. PE 9.3x, PBV 0.88x, DY ~9.7%. Note: ASIAN is the 70% parent of AAI.
ASIAN.business: Integrated food group (founded 1964) producing and exporting processed/frozen seafood under own and OEM brands. BTG.thesis: Integrated agro-food major delivered a strong FY25 (net profit THB6,685m, +171% YoY) but Q1/26 missed hard with net profit -47% YoY to THB1,003m on soft Thai hog prices; a HIGH-flag THB2,000m bond (BTG26525A) maturing 24-May-2026 needs refinancing confirmation.
BTG.summary: Betagro (BTG) is a vertically integrated agro-industrial and food group (feed/Agro, livestock, processed food, pet food, plus regional CLMV/Singapore expansion). Stock trades at 6.6x PE, 1.15x PBV, 7.5% yield. Positives: pet food growth and regional expansion. Watch hog-price recovery and bond refinancing.

CBG.summary: Carabao Group (CBG) is a vertically integrated energy-drink and beverage holding company (also producing its own glass bottles, aluminium cans and packaging). Q1/2026 net profit was THB611.1m on revenue THB5,373.8m, with sales essentially flat YoY (-0.1%) and -6% QoQ; gross profit was THB1,378m at 26% GPM. Management flags Cambodia border tensions as a structural near-to-medium-term risk to that export market, partly offset by improving within-segment beverage GPM (40%->43% YoY). The balance sheet is strong (D/E ~0.38x, operating cash flow THB1,027m in Q1) and the Board approved a treasury-stock repurchase program (May 2026). FS notes flag bond D/E and credit-rating covenants to maintain, plus a THB3,452m impairment allowance on the Carabao Holdings (HK) overseas vehicle. Stock at 18x PE, 2.66x PBV. Watch CLMV/Cambodia recovery and margins.

CPN.thesis: Thailand's leading mall operator delivered record FY2025 core profit (+7%) and a strong Q1/2026 (core profit +27% YoY), with rental's ~90% revenue share and margin expansion the durable engine; only modest near-term refinancing and a flat topline temper the story.

EPG.summary: EPG (March fiscal year-end) posted a strong FY2025/26: net profit rose 62.7% to THB 1,295.1m (EPS THB 0.46) from THB 796.0m, even though revenue was broadly flat at THB 13,705.3m (-2.0% on product sales). The improvement was margin- and efficiency-driven — EBITDA rose to THB 2,613.1m from THB 2,079.4m, gross margin held at ~33.7%, ROE improved to 10.0% (from 6.4%), and operating cash flow more than doubled to THB 2,371.5m. The balance sheet strengthened (D/E 0.55x, current ratio 1.97x). Management highlights growth in the Aeroflex insulation business (electronics, data centers, US market) and planned investments in data-center/electronics/EV themes. The stock has rerated sharply (+95% YTD) to ~12x PE / 1.16x PBV, leaving valuation less of a cushion than a year ago. Net of an unresolved MD&A revision (Yearly figures revised May 2026) and FX/raw-material sensitivity, the trajectory supports a Positive tone.
EPG.business: Holding company investing in innovative polymer/plastic converters across three flagships: Aeroflex (thermal insulation), Aeroklas (automotive accessories), and Eastern Polypack/EPP (plastic packaging); global subsidiaries with significant export exposure.

ESTAR.name: EASTERN STAR REAL ESTATE PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
ESTAR.thesis: Improving but lightly-traded property/golf developer (FY25 net profit up nearly 4x to THB 126m) flagged for a HIGH-severity connected transaction: sale of a condo unit to its own Director/CEO.
ESTAR.summary: ESTAR's operating results improved markedly in FY25 — net profit attributable to equity holders reached THB 126.4m, up nearly 4x from THB 34.1m, as revenue grew 7.1% to THB 2,054.1m and gross margin expanded to 29.4% (from 25.8%) on prudent SG&A control. Q1/2026 added THB 36.5m of net profit. The balance sheet is conservative (D/E 0.43x, current ratio 2.88x), the stock yields ~9.1%, and PBV is just 0.22x. Despite the earnings improvement, the tone is Watch because of a HIGH-severity SET disclosure: a connected transaction involving the sale of a condominium unit to a Director and CEO (filed May 2026, revised days later) — a governance/related-party item requiring scrutiny on pricing and approval. Liquidity is also notable: quick ratio is only 0.16x (most current assets are real-estate inventory) and Q1/26 operating cash flow was negative (-16.9m). The thin float and low absolute price (THB 0.22) limit tradability.
ESTAR.business: Real-estate development for sale and rent plus a golf-course business, with operations concentrated in Bangkok and Rayong Province.

EVER.name: EVERLAND PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
EVER.thesis: Loss-making, highly-leveraged property/hospital developer with a going-concern note and THB 1,927m retained deficit; FY25 loss narrowed but Q1/2026 swung back to a THB 101m loss.
EVER.summary: EVER remains a distressed turnaround. FY25 net loss narrowed to THB 162.5m (NPM -10.5%) from FY24's THB 338.7m, helped by EBITDA turning positive (THB 135.3m vs -11.7m), but the company is still loss-making and Q1/2026 deteriorated sharply to a net loss of THB 101.2m with negative EBITDA (-20.3m). The FS notes carry an explicit going-concern discussion: as at 31 Dec 2025 the Group held a retained deficit of THB 1,926.7m (Company THB 2,314.3m), and statements are prepared on a going-concern basis dependent on management's liquidity and cash-flow plan. Leverage is high (D/E 2.24x at Q1/26) and quick ratio is just 0.06x (asset base is real-estate inventory). Real-estate revenue fell THB 389m YoY. Management's plan is to sell existing inventory (1,415 town-home/commercial units) and non-core assets and to cut costs. With ongoing losses, heavy leverage, and a going-concern flag, EVER stays on Watch.

F&D.thesis: Food processor whose FY25 profit collapsed to near-zero (THB 0.13m from THB 80.6m) on falling export sales, now flagged by a HIGH-severity connected-transaction financial-assistance arrangement.
F&D.summary: F&D is a Watch on two grounds. First, FY25 net profit collapsed to just THB 0.13m from THB 80.6m in FY24 (EPS THB 0.01 vs THB 4.57), as sales fell to THB 581.1m from THB 792.6m, hurt by a decline in sales to Cambodian customers; revenue dropped about 26% and ROE fell to near zero. Second, the company filed a HIGH-severity connected transaction regarding financial assistance (received from a related party, May 2026, revised), alongside a clarification on big-lot share transactions and changes in shareholding structure and the appointment of a new CFO/Chief Accountant — a cluster of governance/ownership and liquidity signals. Q1/2026 net profit was a thin THB 1.4m on THB 98.5m revenue, with negative operating cash flow (-5.5m) and a weak current ratio (0.41x). The balance sheet is otherwise lowly geared (D/E 0.43x) and PBV is 0.59x, but the connected-party financial assistance suggests funding pressure worth close monitoring.

Management guides 2026 revenue growth of 8-12% with a 13-15% gross-margin target and is entering pet food (started ~April 2026). The single-digit profit decline keeps the tone Neutral despite the strong franchise; FX and export risks are the watch items.

FTREIT.thesis: Large industrial REIT (THB ~53bn assets, A/stable) with high occupancy and rising rental income, but net assets from operations fell 14.5% in 6M and recurring leasehold revaluation losses plus a going-concern note on near-term maturities warrant close monitoring.
FTREIT.summary: FTREIT is Thailand's largest industrial freehold-and-leasehold REIT — 745 units, ~THB 53bn portfolio, 2.4mn sqm (392 factories / 353 warehouses), 73% freehold. FY2026 portfolio momentum is healthy: Q1 rental income +9.4%, net profit on investment +11.3%, occupancy 93.7%, gearing 27.9%, ICR 7.31x, average debt cost 3.22%, TRIS A stable, DPU THB 0.1945 (+3.5%). However the F45-clarified bottom line is weaker: net assets from operations fell to THB 691.3mn in Q1/69 (-22.6% YoY) and THB 1,305.2mn in 6M (-14.5% YoY), driven by leasehold fair-value losses (6M FV loss THB 229.3mn vs +138.4mn gain prior year). FS-notes flag a going-concern statement: current-portion liabilities of THB 3,171.7mn vs operating cash, managed via unused facilities, new debentures and additional loans; debenture covenant IBD/total assets <=60% (vs ~28% now, comfortable). Lease expiry of 19% of portfolio in 2569 is the key operational watch.
FTREIT.business: Industrial REIT investing in freehold and leasehold warehouses and factories across Thailand; sponsored and managed by Frasers Property (Thailand). Net-lease structure with tenants bearing most direct costs, supporting high NPI margins.

FUTURERT.thesis: Single-asset retail leasehold REIT on Future Park Rangsit with a high ~9.6% yield and AEI-driven revenue upside, but FY2025 carried a net loss on investments from fair-value decline and a sizeable new asset investment (TUM No.1/2026) is pending unitholder approval.
FUTURERT.summary: FUTURERT invests in leasehold and utilization rights over parts of the Future Park Rangsit retail complex, managed by BBLAM. The trust offers a notably high dividend yield (DY 9.59%) and trades below NAV (PBV 0.89x). 4Q25 total income was THB 263.9mn with net profit on investment THB 118.9mn (+5.5% QoQ), and FY2025 net profit on investment was THB 471.1mn; however 4Q25 also booked a net loss on investments of THB 53.9mn driven by a fair-value decline. December 2025 saw the launch of a revamped/AEI initiative aimed at lifting long-term revenue. The most material near-term catalyst/risk is the 12 Jun 2026 resolution of the Real Estate Investment Committee to pursue additional investment assets, with a Trust Unitholders' Meeting No.1/2026 to be convened — this could be DPU-accretive or dilutive depending on funding (the trust already carries THB 7,355mn total liabilities against THB 12,639mn assets).

GEL.name: GENERAL ENGINEERING PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
GEL.thesis: Distressed construction-materials maker: a THB 0.03 penny stock with chronic net losses (FY2025 -THB 467.2mn, Q1/2026 -THB 89.8mn), negative equity trajectory, current ratio 0.26x and an explicit one-year debt-restructuring plan underpinning a going-concern dependency.
GEL.summary: General Engineering (GEL) manufactures construction materials (prestressed/bored piles, precast, GRC, post-tensioned slabs). The business is in clear distress: FY2025 revenue fell to THB 2,178.0mn (from THB 3,776.2mn in FY2024) with a net loss of THB 467.2mn, and Q1 FY2026 posted a further THB 89.8mn loss on THB 436.5mn revenue (NPM -27%). Liquidity is the central concern — current ratio 0.26x, quick ratio 0.11x, D/E 1.96x — and the FS notes describe a going-concern situation: continuous losses from weak real-estate procurement and delayed infrastructure projects, with management relying on cost cuts (personnel, production efficiency) and a one-year debt restructuring with financial institutions to maintain liquidity and repay debts. The stock is +50% YTD off a tiny base but PBV is only 0.11x, reflecting market scepticism. MD&A also flags impairment losses, price competition and trade-debtor late-payment/liquidity risk.
GEL.business: Producer of prestressed concrete and bored piles, soil-cement columns, precast/segmental concrete, glassfiber-reinforced concrete, chemical construction products and post-tensioned slabs, serving Thailand's property and infrastructure sectors.

GFPT.name: GFPT PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
GFPT.thesis: Integrated poultry exporter grew FY2025 net profit +24% on margin expansion despite soft UK exports, with a near-debt-free balance sheet; the main watch is heavy reliance on related-party (family) loans for 56% of total debt.
GFPT.summary: GFPT is Positive. FY2025 net profit rose ~24% to THB 2,439.4mn (from THB 1,973.8mn) even as revenue slipped slightly to THB 19,205.5mn (-2.3%), as gross margin expanded to 16.35% from 13.82% (EBIT margin per oppday). Q1/2026 continued the trend with net profit THB 517.1mn (NPM 11.9%) on revenue THB 4,357.8mn and a very strong balance sheet — D/E 0.28x, current ratio 4.65x. The most material flag is MED: long-term related-party (Sirimongkolkasem family) loans of THB 3,470.25mn equal 56.27% of total liabilities, plus THB 230mn short-term RP loans, raising questions on terms and minority fairness. Other MEDs: GFN (GFPT Nichirei) associate profit fell 41.65% to THB 187.31mn, and total chicken export volume dropped 9.84% (-3,600 tonnes) led by UK weakness, dragging Food segment revenue -7.64%. The 2025FY digest recommends escalation to a 6-Theme Health Check on the RPT debt structure. Trades at a low PE 4.62 / PBV 0.49 with DY 2.34, down 19.3% YTD. 2026 revenue guidance is +2-3%.
GFPT.business: GFPT runs a vertically integrated poultry operation — feed mill, breeder/hatchery/broiler farms, evisceration and processed food. Main products: cooked chicken, fresh/frozen chicken, processed food, and land/aquatic animal feed. 45-year operating history; targets Net Zero by 2050.

A chief-accountant change (29 May 2026) and an ongoing minority-shareholding-distribution program are also in play.

ITC.name: i-Tail Corporation Public Company Limited
ITC.thesis: Leading Thai pet-food OEM is still growing USD sales strongly (Q1/2026 +28.6% YoY), but FY2025 reported net profit fell 17.2% on margin erosion, and Pillar Two global-minimum-tax plus US-tariff assumptions threaten 2026 earnings.
ITC.summary: ITC warrants Watch despite strong topline momentum. Q1/2026 was robust: revenue THB 5,309.5mn (THB sales +21.8% YoY, USD sales +28.6% to USD 163mn), net profit THB 871.3mn (NPM 16.4%), with GPM solid at 24.3%. However, FY2025 reported net profit fell 17.2% YoY to THB 2,977.9mn as GPM dropped 2.6pts to 25.1% on US-tariff support given to customers, SG&A +15.3%, and baht strength compressing THB revenue. The most material flag is MED Pillar Two (BEPS 2.0): ITC falls under the global minimum tax via Thai Union Group, with effective tax expected to rise 5-7% in 2026 — a direct hit to net profit. The full-year outlook assumes a 19% US tariff and 32.5 THB/USD; either changing would force re-estimation. FY2025 inventory rose 22.7% to THB 4,338mn vs only 2.8% THB sales growth (days inventory 103→110). The balance sheet is pristine (D/E 0.14x, current ratio 8.0x). 2026 guidance: USD sales +9-12%, GPM 23-25%. DY 5.35%, PE 15.04.
ITC.business: i-Tail Corporation (ITC) is a leading Thai OEM/private-label manufacturer of pet food, principally wet cat/dog food plus a fast-growing Pet Treats line. Key markets: Americas (~58%), Asia-Oceania (~28%), Europe (~14%). Part of the Thai Union group; Thailand is the largest wet-pet-food exporter to the US (~30% of US import value).

ITD.name: ITALIAN-THAI DEVELOPMENT PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
ITD.thesis: Distressed large-cap contractor: a going-concern note remains in the FY2025 statements, D/E is ~24x on wafer-thin equity, Q1/2026 swung back to a Baht 220.7m net loss, and liquidity is critically tight (current ratio 0.70, quick 0.24).
ITD.summary: ITALIAN-THAI DEVELOPMENT is a major one-stop construction contractor whose balance sheet is severely stretched. FY2025 reported a Baht 1,783.3m group net profit — but this was driven by revenue de-recognition of an overseas subsidiary and other non-operating items, not core recovery (gross margin was negative -16.5% at the full-year line). Q1/2026 reversed to a net loss of Baht 220.7m on revenue of Baht 7,911.3m, with operating cash flow of only Baht 527.4m. Equity is just Baht 3,083.6m against total liabilities of Baht 79,412.0m (D/E ~24x), and liquidity is critical (current ratio 0.70, quick 0.24). The FY2025 notes carry an explicit going-concern discussion: management is pursuing funding initiatives, executing revised business plans, and managing debt payments to support the going-concern basis. The 2026 AGM initially lacked quorum and was rescheduled as an E-AGM. The stock has rallied YTD (+30.8%) but at Baht 0.34 trades at 0.58x book — a high-risk turnaround/restructuring situation.
ITD.business: One of Thailand's largest general construction contractors with broad civil, infrastructure and advanced-construction capability, plus soil/coal extraction and construction-support services through subsidiaries.

J.name: JAS ASSET PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
J.thesis: JAS Asset's property arm is deeply loss-making — FY2025 net loss THB 785mn (mostly non-cash FV writedowns) and a critically low 0.08x current ratio — even as the parent Jaymart group it sits inside shows a turnaround.
J.summary: J (the listed entity here is JAS Asset, the property arm) is a clear Watch. Q1/2026 net loss was THB -62.2mn (NPM -34.7%) on revenue THB 179.4mn, with the 2026Q1 digest flagging two HIGHs: a current ratio of 0.08x (acute short-term liquidity risk) and a net loss that widened 102.5% YoY, driven mainly by fair-value losses on investment property. FY2025 was worse — net loss THB 785mn (vs THB 165.6mn profit in 2024, a 574% swing) from THB 550.5mn FV loss on investment property and THB 116.4mn asset impairment, both largely non-cash; year-end cash was only THB 12.1mn and finance cost rose 32.2% to THB 163.7mn. D/E is 1.09x. Note that the Jaymart Group Holdings oppday (the broader listed group) shows a turnaround — group FY2025 net profit THB 1,169mn (+28%) and Q1/2026 group profit THB 163mn (+16%) led by JMB, KBJ, SINGER and SGC — but JAS Asset itself remains the drag. Recent disclosures include a paid-up capital increase, J-W3/J-W4 warrant exercises and J-W4 trading suspension. KAM centers on rental revenue recognition.
J.business: The context profiles two layers. The listed financials are JAS Asset PCL — rental-space management for mobile/IT retail ('IT Junction'), community markets ('J Market') and community malls ('The Jas'). It sits within Jaymart Group Holdings, a diversified holding (JMB phone retail, JMT debt collection, Jaymart Mobile MVNO, JAS Asset, J Ventures, SINGER/SGC consumer finance).

JCK.name: JCK INTERNATIONAL PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
JCK.thesis: Property developer is in distress — FY2025 revenue collapsed 70% and swung to a THB 387mn loss, with THB 3,843mn of bonds/loans (55% of debt) in payment default and under restructuring, plus an unsettled THB 2.7bn related-party hotel acquisition.
JCK.summary: JCK is a clear Watch. FY2025 total revenue fell 70.17% to THB 652.3mn and swung to a net loss of THB 386.7mn (from a THB 173.6mn profit), driven by a severe contraction in industrial-estate land sales. Q1/2026 stayed deeply loss-making: net loss THB -117.6mn (NPM -82.0%) on revenue of just THB 143.5mn, with D/E at 2.77x. The most severe flags are HIGH: bonds and loans of THB 3,843mn (55% of total liabilities) entered payment default during the year and require restructuring with banks and bondholders across multiple bond series; the auditor notes default interest demanded by an asset seller. A MED/EOM 'draw attention' covers the THB 2,709mn related-party acquisition of the JC Kevin Sathorn Bangkok hotel — control taken from 16 May 2025 but legal title not yet transferred, with the second payment tranche extended to 31 Mar 2026. The auditor also flags THB 8,219mn (85% of group assets) at high impairment risk. The 2026Q1 digest explicitly recommends escalation to a 6-Theme Health Check. Trades at THB 0.14, PBV 0.21.

JDF.thesis: Small-cap food-seasoning maker compounding steadily: Q1/2026 net profit Baht 35.2m with GPM expanding to 37.2%, FY2025 net profit +8.7%, net-cash balance sheet (D/E 0.33) and a 9.2% yield.
JDF.summary: JD Food produces and distributes food seasonings, sauces, fillings and dehydrated products (25+ years, OEM-led). Momentum is positive: Q1/2026 revenue Baht 221.8m delivered net profit Baht 35.2m (NPM 15.9%) with gross margin expanding to 37.2% from the FY2025 level of 32.5%. FY2025 net profit rose ~8.7% to Baht 86.6m on revenue of Baht 737.5m (+10.9% YoY), continuing FY2024's strong run. The balance sheet is conservative — net-cash, D/E 0.33, current ratio 2.1 — and ROE improved to ~14% in Q1. The Opp Day highlighted OEM-driven growth in snack seasonings, supplements and HoReCa, cost discipline lifting net profit, and 2026 expansion plans targeting Asia-Pacific (notably oyster/bean products) plus new distribution partners. PB.name: PRESIDENT BAKERY PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
PB.thesis: Dominant, cash-rich Farmhouse bakery franchise with a fortress balance sheet, but earnings are in a multi-period downtrend—FY2025 net profit -20.9% and Q1-2026 -13.4%—as cost inflation (minimum wage, depreciation from new capex) erodes gross margin while sales decline.

The story is quality-defensive but the earnings direction and margin-cost squeeze warrant the Watch tag; a single subsidiary's segment/RPT detail is not yet visible in the file set.

PQS.name: Premier Quality Starch Public Company Limited
PQS.thesis: Tapioca-starch turnaround story that swung to a FY25 net loss on a ~22% price collapse and China-demand weakness; HIGH flags on a regulatory plant shutdown and a prior-year restatement, plus SET-queried Q1 MD&A, keep this firmly on Watch despite an ungeared balance sheet.
PQS.summary: PQS swung from a FY2024 net profit of THB 241.1mn to a FY2025 net loss of THB 79.1mn (NPM -4.0%), as sales fell 27.9% YoY to THB 1,953.4mn — volume was nearly flat (-0.2%) but average selling price dropped over 22% on structural Chinese-demand pressure. Q1/2026 returned to a thin net profit of THB 19.8mn (NPM 3.0%, GPM 13.2%) but operating cash flow was negative THB 155.2mn as working capital was absorbed. The FY25 digest carries two HIGH flags: a government-ordered shutdown of the Kalasin plant (9 Sep-18 Dec 2025) to fix wastewater/steam systems, hitting >3 months of capacity, and a 2024 restatement of inventory NRV allowance and JV profit share. Management guides aggressive FY2026 targets (+40% revenue, 20% GP margin) contingent on starch prices, China orders and Kalasin ramp — all partly outside its control. No FY25 dividend. SET queried the Q1/2026 MD&A (high-severity, 22 May).
PQS.business: Premier Quality Starch manufactures and sells native and modified tapioca starch (capacity ~300k tpa native, ~45k tpa modified) across four plants in Mukdahan, Sakon Nakhon and the new Kalasin facility, with side businesses in biogas electricity and newly launched transport/logistics.

Strategy levers: increase higher-margin modified-starch mix, low-carbon starch program to 2573, and an MOU with Sojitz + Kaset DX for sustainable cassava sourcing.
Thailand's 19% reciprocal tariff (from 1 Aug 2025) is lower than China's, a relative competitive positive.

PROSPECT.name: PROSPECT LOGISTICS AND INDUSTRIAL FREEHOLD AND LEASEHOLD REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST
PROSPECT.thesis: Growing industrial/logistics REIT with high occupancy (~99-100%), positive rental reversion (6-9% per 3-yr renewal), two FY2025 capital raises lifting revenue ~46% YoY, and a ~7.6% yield — now moving to monthly distributions.
PROSPECT.summary: PROSPECT REIT owns factories and warehouses for rent across five projects (Bangkok Free Trade Zone 1/2/3/6 and X44 Bangna KM.18), totaling 564,758 sqm of leasable area. The trust grew materially through two FY2025 capital increases: FY2025 total revenue rose to THB877.3m from THB599.4m (+46%), and total assets nearly doubled to THB10,053.9m from THB5,359.3m as the asset base expanded. Q1-2026 revenue was THB297.9m on total assets THB10,064.5m and liabilities THB4,501.5m. Operating fundamentals are strong: oppday disclosed BFTZ1 occupancy of 99.14% (others ~100%), rental reversion of ~6-9% per 3-year renewal cycle and ~2.5-3%/year step-ups on new leases, with DPU of THB0.8280 (+11.92% QoQ) and gearing (D/E) ~88%. The trust trades at 1.07x P/BV (a premium to most peers) with a ~7.57% DY and was +33% YTD. In Apr-2026 it shifted cash distributions from quarterly to monthly. The main watch items are gearing, FY2026 lease-expiry renewals among top tenants, and the BFTZ4 development pipeline.

Managed by Prospect REIT Management Co., Ltd.

PROUD.name: PROUD REAL ESTATE PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
PROUD.thesis: Turnaround property developer: FY2025 revenue jumped ~183% to THB6.41bn and net profit ~196% to THB167.8m as projects were delivered and debt repaid (net D/E down to ~1.9 from 3.3), backed by a THB6.1bn backlog and a ~9.9% dividend yield at 0.5x P/BV.
PROUD.summary: PROUD (Proud Real Estate) is a property developer with landed, condo and special/hospitality projects concentrated in Bangkok, Hua Hin and Phuket. FY2025 was a breakout year: total revenue surged to THB6,409.6m from THB2,272.1m (+183%) and net profit rose to THB167.8m from THB56.6m (+196%), as large project transfers (e.g., New District R9, Wana, the 'Rom'/Conance project) were recognized. Crucially, deleveraging was dramatic — FY2025 generated THB1,931m of operating cash flow used to repay debt (financing -THB1,934.6m), cutting balance-sheet D/E to 3.32 (from 5.81) and reported net D/E to ~1.9 (oppday). Q1-2026 stayed profitable: revenue THB1,265.0m, EBITDA THB94.6m, net profit THB54.4m, EPS THB0.06, with strong operating cash flow of THB428.9m. Management cites a THB6.1bn backlog (~84% high-certainty) and FY2026 revenue-recognition target of ~THB5.6bn. The stock trades at 5.62x P/E, 0.5x P/BV and a ~9.89% DY. Leverage, though much improved, remains high (D/E 3.11 at Q1) and is the principal watch item.
PROUD.business: Real-estate developer (Proud Real Estate) with a diversified portfolio of landed housing, condominiums and special/hospitality-oriented projects in high-demand locations (Bangkok, Hua Hin, Phuket); revenue is project-transfer driven, supported by a sales backlog.

PSH.name: PRUKSA HOLDING PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
PSH.thesis: PSH swung to a FY2025 net loss of THB 540mn (from +456mn in 2024) on a 29% revenue collapse and a still-soft property market; Q1/2026 returned to a thin THB 56mn profit but the recovery is unproven.
PSH.summary: Pruksa Holding is a diversified property-and-healthcare holding company whose core residential business remains under pressure from a subdued Bangkok housing market. FY2025 revenue fell to THB 14,983mn from THB 20,996mn (-28.6%) and the group posted a net loss of THB 540mn versus a THB 456mn profit in 2024, with EPS of -0.25. EBITDA compressed sharply to THB 584mn from THB 1,995mn. Q1/2026 showed a tentative turn: revenue THB 3,430mn, net profit THB 56mn (EPS 0.03), but margins remain thin (NPM 1.9%). The balance sheet is comfortable (D/E 0.46x, net D/E ~0.28x per oppday) and the stock trades at a deep 0.19x P/BV with a 3.2% yield. Management is re-shaping the portfolio, leaning on the healthcare arm and a Capital Land JV (revenue expected Q3). Q1/2026 presales rose 12% but transfers fell 12%, signalling a soft conversion pipeline.
PSH.business: Holding company (ex-Pruksa Real Estate) developing single-detached houses, townhouses and condominiums in Bangkok and surrounding provinces, plus a growing private healthcare (hospital) arm and selected JV investments (incl. Capital Land and General Engineering).

PYLON.name: PYLON PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
PYLON.thesis: Specialist foundation/piling contractor in a clean, strongly improving cycle — FY25 net profit rebounded to THB 210.8mn from near-zero, margins are recovering, and an all-time-high backlog of THB 2,148mn underpins 2026 growth.
PYLON.summary: PYLON delivered a sharp earnings recovery: FY2025 net profit of THB 210.8mn vs just THB 0.5mn in FY2024, on revenue THB 1,501.7mn (+83% YoY), with GP margin up to 22.9% from 19.3% and ROE ~20%. Q1/2026 continued strong — revenue THB 490.3mn, net profit THB 77.3mn (NPM 15.8%, GPM 23.7%), ROE ~25%, D/E 0.39x and current ratio 3.43x. The FY25 digest found no HIGH or MED flags; the only note is a LOW KAM on percentage-of-completion revenue recognition, and the financials are described as clean. Backlog stood at THB 2,148mn as of 25 Feb 2026 (all-time high since the 2002 founding and above full-year FY25 revenue), supported by demand from MRT Orange Line and infrastructure work. With a 7.27% dividend yield, a lightly geared balance sheet and visible backlog, tone is Positive; the main watch is competition and revenue-recognition judgement. Note RM coverage is Kae, not Champ.

Q-CON.name: QUALITY CONSTRUCTION PRODUCTS PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
Q-CON.thesis: Q-CON's FY2025 net profit halved to THB 249mn (from THB 504mn, -50.6%) on a 22% sales drop tied to weak construction demand and falling AAC prices; Q1/2026 stabilised but the stock sits at its 52-week low.
Q-CON.summary: Quality Construction Products (LH-affiliated AAC maker) saw earnings cut roughly in half in FY2025: net profit THB 248.8mn vs THB 503.7mn (-50.6%) as sales revenue fell 22% on lower autoclaved-aerated-concrete volumes and prices. GPM compressed to 26.3% from 33.0% and ROE fell to 9.1% from 18.7%. The balance sheet stays very clean (D/E 0.15x, current ratio 4.6x, net cash). Q1/2026 looks steadier — revenue THB 466mn, net profit THB 50.3mn, NPM 10.8%, EBITDA margin ~21% — suggesting the worst of the price/volume decline may be passing, though revenue is still soft versus 2024. Valuation is undemanding (P/E ~11.5x, P/BV 0.93x) with a high 6.6% dividend yield, but the shares are at a 52-week low and YTD -6.9%. This is a Watch on the >50% profit decline despite the pristine balance sheet.
Q-CON.business: Manufacturer and distributor of autoclaved aerated concrete (AAC) products — blocks, lintels, wall/floor panels and stairs — spun off from Land & Houses (LH); demand is geared to Thai residential and commercial construction activity.

SAPPE.summary: Sappe (SAPPE) is a leading Thai innovative-beverage company with five product categories and a heavily export-tilted revenue mix. Management guides ~15% full-year revenue growth (to ~THB 6,041mn) with Q2 as high season. Valuation is supportive at PE ~12.5x, PBV ~2.0x, with a ~5.8% yield. The two-period earnings decline keeps the tone at Watch.

STI.summary: STI's results are mixed against a tough public-sector backdrop. Balance sheet is reasonable (D/E 0.96x, current ratio 2.16x).

TFM.thesis: High-ROE aquafeed producer (Thai Union Feedmill) with strong growth, record FY2025 earnings and ~9% dividend yield; key watch items are surging fishmeal costs and a large new Ecuador investment.
TFM.summary: TFM is clearly improving. FY2025 net profit rose to THB 733.2mn (from THB 535.4mn) on revenue THB 6,094.9mn (+12.2%), with FY gross margin expanding to 22.2% (from 18.7%) and ROE a strong 29.0%. The balance sheet is excellent (D/E 0.34x, current ratio 3.19x, quick ratio 2.43x), supporting a ~9.3% dividend yield at PE 8.61x. The freshest flags are MED-level, not HIGH: fishmeal (key raw material) jumped +31.2% YoY to THB 47.18/kg, pressuring margins if cost pass-through lags; and the board approved an Ecuador aquaculture investment of up to USD 55mn (~2.5yr build, no near-term return). FY2025 also saw bad-debt expense surge +96.1% (THB 28mn→55mn) — KPMG flagged trade-receivable ECL as a KAM — and the 51% sale of AMG-TFM (Pakistan) deconsolidated that unit. Overall trajectory is positive with monitorable cost/capex risks.

TTCL.summary: TTCL provides integrated EPC (design, procurement, construction) for petroleum, petrochemical and chemical plants in Thailand and overseas. FY2025 produced a net loss of THB 6,199.5mn (EPS -10.06) and a gross loss, with EBITDA -THB 5,730mn, driven by THB 4,555mn of expected credit losses and asset impairments. Equity is negative at -THB 3,873.8mn (Q1-2026 -THB 3,888.2mn) against THB 15.07bn liabilities. Coverage is monitoring of the rehabilitation outcome and recoveries for stakeholders, not valuation.

WHART.summary: WHA Premium Growth Freehold and Leasehold REIT (WHART) is a large industrial REIT (total assets THB54.3bn, market cap THB37.5bn) holding warehouses, factories and built-to-suit assets in Thai logistics clusters, sponsored by WHA Corporation. Q1/2026 revenue was THB857.7m. The units trade at THB10.80 (PBV 1.02x, trailing yield 6.27%). Quality assets (e.g. WGCL IDC Rayong: 100% occupancy, single 30-year built-to-suit tenant with 10% escalation every 3 years) underpin predictable income. FY2025 revenue fell to THB729.8m (-6.62% from THB781.5m) and net profit dropped to THB35.2m from THB52.8m (-33%) on a higher administrative cost base, even as gross margin held near 28.8%. Q1/2026 stabilised somewhat: revenue THB201.5m, net profit THB11.9m, GPM 29.0%, NPM 5.9%. The balance sheet is very clean — D/E 0.18x, current ratio 4.45x, quick ratio 2.70x, equity THB917.3m and minimal debt. Valuation is full at PE ~19x though PBV is 0.71x with a 4.11% yield. The key governance item is a HIGH-severity connected transaction (announced 7 May, revised 8 May 2026) to acquire operational-support software from a related party, plus the dissolution of a subsidiary — both warrant scrutiny on pricing and rationale. With falling profit and a related-party acquisition, this sits at Watch despite financial strength.

XBIO.name: X BIOSCIENCE PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
XBIO.thesis: Loss-making food/restaurant investor with multiple HIGH flags — going-concern uncertainty, a SET 'CB' sign, THB 1,845mn accumulated losses, a THB -335.9mn Q1/2026 loss and sub-1.0 liquidity — now relying on dilutive capital increases and warrants to survive.
XBIO.summary: XBIO is in distress. The Q1/2026 digest carries three simultaneous HIGH flags: a net loss of THB -335.9mn (NPM -394.6%) despite revenue growth of 55.7% YoY — signalling large non-operating/extraordinary charges; an auditor Emphasis of Matter on going-concern uncertainty from prolonged accumulated losses; and a current ratio of 0.97x (below 1.0). The FY2025 digest is equally severe: going-concern plus a SET 'CB' sign (equity fell below 50% of paid-up capital), consolidated accumulated losses of THB 1,845.28mn, FY2025 net loss THB 452.49mn (+72.66% YoY) on revenue down 59.42% to THB 129.55mn, negative operating cash flow of THB -75.29mn, and THB 256.75mn of impairments in one year. The company is responding with a bundled BOD recapitalisation (capital increase, XBIO-W9 warrants to existing shareholders, board/CFO changes, EGM 2/2026) and the 'CC' sign was lifted on 2 Jun 2026 — but dilution and survival risk dominate.
XBIO.business: X Bioscience — a holding company invested in the food business, principally restaurants (closing low-potential branches). Market cap ~THB 972mn; price THB 0.08; PBV 3.0x. Equity below 50% of paid-up capital (SET 'CB' sign).

ZEN.name: ZEN CORPORATION GROUP PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
ZEN.thesis: Restaurant holding company whose core dining business keeps shrinking (SSSG -6.4%, restaurant revenue -9% FY2025), partly offset by fast-growing Manufacturing & Trading and franchise — net margin remains razor-thin at ~1.2% and a +224% tax jump cut FY2025 profit 15%.
ZEN.summary: ZEN's FY2025 showed structural pressure in its core: revenue fell 3% to THB 3,979.4mn, restaurant revenue dropped THB 296mn (-9% YoY) with SSSG -6.4%, and gross margin slipped to 39.1% (-1.2pp). Net profit fell to THB 45.8mn from THB 56.9mn (-19% / digest -15%), even though group pre-tax profit rose +6% — because income tax jumped +224% YoY (THB 8mn→THB 27mn), a MED flag warranting a deferred-tax review. Offsetting the dining weakness, Manufacturing & Trading grew +25% to THB 918mn (5-year CAGR 73%) and franchise +25%, diversifying earnings. Q1/2026 was a soft positive: net profit THB 15.7mn (reportedly +23% YoY) on revenue THB 941.2mn (NPM 2.6%), consistent with a profitability-over-growth, asset-light franchise strategy. Goodwill of THB 255.37mn is a Key Audit Matter exposed to further dining contraction. FY2026 targets SSSG +3-5%, which looks demanding against a ~1.5-2.0% GDP backdrop.
ZEN.business: ZEN Corporation Group — a holding company over restaurant brands (ZEN Japanese, Tummour, Bar B Q Plaza, Khiang) plus franchise (ZKC, international) and a Manufacturing & Trading arm selling packaged food products. Market cap ~THB 1.6bn; PE 32.7x, PBV 1.17x, yield 1.87%.
